Wed, 26 Aug 2026 23:29:48 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1 https://beesayatv.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-09-32x32.png Tough – beesayatv https://beesayatv.com/ 32 32 Camp 8 to Matun-og Falls Hike (Updated) | Camp 8, Guindaruhan-Crasher Site | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/camp-8-to-matun-og-falls-hike-anxiety-took-over-camp-8-minglanilla-2026-gpx/ Sat, 04 Jul 2026 10:38:04 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=487 The Camp 8 to Matun-og Falls trail is a 5.72-kilometer point-to-point community route in Minglanilla, passing through farms, local settlements, and the valley leading toward Matun-og Falls. I hiked it in August 2026, starting from Camp 8 and approaching the falls from the opposite direction of the more commonly used Guindaruhan–Taboan–Crasher Site route.

Although the distance is relatively short, I dealt with repeated climbs and descents along the way. This was my second attempt from Camp 8, and this time I reached Matun-og Falls.

Trail Snapshot

TOUGH
DocumentedAugust 2026
Distance5.72 km (Point-to-Point)

This 5.72 km hike involves a total elevation gain of approximately 255 m, spanning altitudes from 55 m to 494 m, with smoothed maximum grades reaching roughly +31% uphill and -29% downhill, and its toughest climb occurring right out of the gate in the first kilometer (km 0.3–0.6).

Duration3 - 3.5 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeLimited
Surface100% trail

Reception available from the trailhead down to the upper ridge, but drops into a dead zone during descent into Matun-og gorge and across the entire river trek, reconnecting near the crasher exit.

GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I parked my motorcycle along the concrete road near the jump-off point, where there was no parking fee. Private vehicles can reach the area, while public transportation is limited. Habal-habal service is also available.

Why this trail is rated Tough

✓ Significant endurance required
✓ Sustained steep ascent or descent
✓ Limited or no mobile signal
✓ Navigation requires attention
✓ Limited bailout options

On this trail: farmland • river crossing • valley

Route Description

From the jump-off point, I immediately started on a short but steep climb toward the top of the mountain. Locals use this trail regularly, so much of the route is well-trodden.

Early in the ascent, I followed a cemented staircase. Some sections were already missing, but the remaining steps made that part of the climb easier.

As I continued, I passed farmland planted with corn and camote. I also saw cows, goats, and a few carabaos along the route.

The trail passes through several local communities, including settlements deeper in the valley. Other sections felt more isolated because dense vegetation blocked much of the surrounding view.

Later, I descended toward the river that feeds Matun-og Falls. That section gave me the most difficulty because of the steep slope and loose surface.

Trail Conditions

The morning was sunny, and it had not rained for several days. I found the trail very dry, with loose soil that became particularly slippery during the descent toward the river. Based on the condition noted for this route, the same trail can become muddy and slippery after rain.

Shade was limited during the hike, and I did not pass any stores along the route. I encountered locals but few insects. Mobile signal was limited or absent in some sections.

There is also a significant section of river trekking before reaching Matun-og Falls. During this hike, the river section was passable, but this part of the route could become dangerous during heavy rain or a sudden rise in water level.

Additional Notes

Most hikers taking this connection travel in the opposite direction, coming from Matun-og Falls and climbing toward Camp 8. On the steep section I descended, climbing would have been easier than going down on the dry, loose soil.

For the exact route I followed, a trekking pole would have helped with the descent. I carried the expectation of needing at least two liters of water because of the limited shade and the repeated climbs and descents.

]]> Bitlang Trail Loop | Sudlon 1, Cebu City | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/bitlang-trail-loop/ Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:03:27 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=205 The Bitlang Trail is a documented 5.3 km point-to-point hike that starts in Sitio Tabla, Sudlon 1, Cebu City, and descends to Bonbon. I followed the descending section of the trail through farms, small mountain communities, and river sections before reaching the valley.

The terrain remained easy to follow throughout the hike, although some sections were uneven and rocky. This report covers only the downhill portion of the route, while the sustained climb back to Sitio Tabla forms part of a separate full-loop hike. I completed this hike in June 2026.

Trail Snapshot

TOUGH
DocumentedJune 2026
Distance12.89 km (Loop)
Duration6-7 hrs
WaterAt least 3 liters
ShadeModerate
Surface60% trail, 40% road
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near the covered court in Sitio Tabla, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. V-hires operated along the Transcentral Highway route, while habal-habal services were also available.

Why this trail is rated Tough

✓ Long hiking distance requiring sustained endurance
✓ Long or sustained climbs and descents
✓ Prolonged physical effort over several hours
✓ High route commitment with limited bailout options
✓ Assistance or evacuation may take considerable time

On this trail: farmland • forest • ridge • valley • viewpoint

Route Description

I began the hike by descending through narrow trails that gradually led toward the valley. The route passed farms, small settlements, and several river sections before reaching Bonbon. Navigation remained straightforward, although some stretches became uneven and rocky underfoot.

This report ends at the river near Bonbon. The return climb from Buot-Taup back to Sitio Tabla was not part of this hike and is covered separately. That ascent completes the full 13 km loop and consists of a sustained uphill climb lasting about 4 km.

Trail Conditions

Clouds covered the area throughout my hike. Rain the night before left the trail slightly muddy, although walking conditions remained manageable. Most of the route was exposed with limited tree cover, while stores were available whenever I passed through communities. Mobile signal started out strong before disappearing later in the hike. I did not encounter any other hikers, and mosquitoes were present in areas with denser vegetation.

Additional Notes

Although this section of the Bitlang Trail is relatively easy, completing the full loop requires enough water for the long return climb. I carried 3 liters, and I found stores between the Bitlang exit and the start of the uphill section. A trekking pole or walking stick can help with balance on the uneven terrain and reduce strain on the knees.

On sunny days, an umbrella is also useful because much of the trail has little shade. The entire route has no dangerous cliffs or exposed ridges.
